requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints` has no implementation roots, and none is needed. Its clauses describe observable hashing behavior, not how the code is built.

- **"Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words"**: SHA-256 is part of the output, not an internal choice. A different digest or library would produce different hash values, so this clause is a behavioral one. An implementation that used another SHA-256 library would still produce the same hashes and still conform. The encoding rules come from the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which supplies context and is not judged here.
- **"The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version"**: this fixes the value the scheme reports. The `fingerprint_scheme` signature belongs to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, so it is not an obligation of this text.
- **"HTML comment blocks are excluded"; "Inline HTML comments within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text"; "Paragraph and directive prose uses word-based hashing"**: these state what the hash input contains and how it is hashed. Any code that produces the same hashes satisfies them.
- **"Reflowing whitespace ... preserves the hash"; "Changing its words changes the structural encoding"**: these are input-to-output properties of the hash, so they are behavioral.

The text names no required library, type, field, signature or delegation interface. The `Implements` edges on the requirement are empty, which matches this. Tests cover the behavioral clauses.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover every observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints`.

- **SHA-256 structural hash.** `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts that the markdown fingerprint is 64 hex characters. The prescribed digest is an implementation choice, so a length-and-format check is enough.
- **Fingerprint scheme.** `check`, the helper reached from `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline`, asserts `markdown-structural-v1` through `language.fingerprint_scheme()`. It also asserts that the loaded `OutlineContent` retains that scheme.
- **HTML comment blocks excluded.** `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile` (a.md case) and `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` (a.md case) check this. Changing a block comment's text, or removing the comment, keeps the section hash. Changing a non-comment word changes it.
- **Inline comments stay paragraph text.** `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows the inline comment is not a comment, and the owner is a `paragraph`. `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` shows that editing an inline comment (`one` to `two`) changes the fingerprint.
- **Word-based hashing of paragraph and directive prose.**
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` asserts that `ab cd` differs from `abcd`.
  - `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` asserts that added words change the hash and extra spaces do not.
  - `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` covers directive prose.
- **Reflow preserves the hash.**
  - `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` covers moving line breaks within a paragraph.
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` covers leading and trailing whitespace.
  - `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` covers directive reflow.
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` covers reflow of nested directive paragraphs with the surrounding structure unchanged.
- **Changing words changes the encoding.** `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` (`brownfox`), `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` (replacement text), and `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` all show a changed hash.

I found no obligation that lacks a test or an assertion.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
